Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
DragonCon 2004 will take place in Atlanta, Georgia from September 3rd
thru September 6th.

http://www.dragoncon.org/

The following V:TES events will be run during the convention:

Friday 1 pm - 9 pm
V:TES World of Darkness Draft
Fee unlisted
Description: V:EKN sanctioned booster draft tournament. A mixed (but
fixed) assortment of 8 boosters per player. Two rounds plus a final.
(2.5 hour final round starts at 6pm). Additional Master: Discipline
cards will be provided, up to 2 per player.

Saturday 9 am - 6 pm
V:TES Dragon's Breath Tournament
Fee $dragoncon decided (probably 3)
Expect 40-50 players (10 tables)
Description: V:EKN sanctioned constructed deck tournament. Three
rounds plus a final (the final starts at 5pm?).

Sunday 9 am - 12 noon
V:TES Demo and Rapid Thought Tournaments
Fee $dragoncon decided (probably 3)
Expect 10-30 players
Description: Demos for new players and continuous 9 player Rapid
Thought tournaments as they fill up. Rapid Thought follows standard
V:EKN rules except that each round is 45 minutes, libraries must be 60
cards, and the banned list is extended to include: Minion Tap, Blood
Doll, and Tribute to the Master.

Sunday 1 pm - 8 pm
Fee $dragoncon decided (probably 3)
Expect 15-25 players
Description: Unsanctioned constructed deck tournament. Create your
own vampires for your 12-card crypt. See construction parameters at:
http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/cac.html

Monday 9 am - 4 pm
Fee $dragoncon decided (probably 3)
Description: Bring your own mix-n-match selection of 9 booster packs
from any White Wolf sets (11 card boosters only, that is). Additional
Master: Discipine cards will be provided, up to 2 per player.
Remember: the grouping rule is not used in sealed deck tournaments.
Two rounds plus a final (the final round starts at 2 pm).

Messages.Author: Curevei
Messages.Body:
>OK. It's up.
>http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/cac.html

I'll skip with criticisms of the point method since that has never gotten me
anywhere before. While I'm sure this will get ignored as well, I think the
last prize is a bad idea. I've always found that doling out prizes based on
who makes games fun is exceedingly unfair, for instance more gregarious
personalities are far more likely to win, and tends to produce behavior that
may be not be desirable such as playing to be fun rather than playing to win
(in this case, possibly something more likely in the later rounds when people
don't think they will make the finals).

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:


While your critisizim of a prize for being "fun" is in no way invalid
in a general sense, the whole "create your own clan" event is a
completely absurdist venture from the get go, and as such, splitting
hairs between "playing to win" and "playing to be fun" is mostly
irrelevant.

I don't think anyone who is going to be invoved in the create a clan
event is going to be in the least bit concerened with winning the
event overall, and the whole exercise will be one of, pretty much,
pure gag material (i.e. the whole event will be lighthearted and no
one will really care who wins).

I'd see your point is highly valid if there were, say, prizes for
"most fun player" in a sanctioned tournament. Create a clan, however,
is not a sanctioned tournament, and is mostly intended to be funny.

-Peter
